# ig-design-system

> Infragistics design system: design tokens generated with igniteui-theming, plus the checks that keep sites consistent. This file is generated by `src/llms.ts` on every build; do not edit it.

One design system for the Infragistics sites. It ships CSS custom properties and the checks that keep a site on them. It has no components and no JavaScript a page loads.

## Using it in a site

```sh
npm install ig-design-system
```

Load the stylesheets in this order, before the site's own styles:

1. `ig-design-system/fonts.css` — optional. The three faces. Leave it out when the site already loads Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans and JetBrains Mono.
2. `ig-design-system/tokens.css` — every token with its default value.
3. `ig-design-system/theme.css` — the live layer: dials, derived state colours, the dark variant, type roles.
4. `ig-design-system/base.css` — optional. Element styles for a site that has none.

```css
@import 'ig-design-system/fonts.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/tokens.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/theme.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/base.css';
```

A documentation site puts `data-igd-type="docs"` on `<html>` for the smaller type set. `data-theme="dark"` selects the dark variant.

## Rules for code that uses the tokens

1. **Choose a colour by its job.** Text, a background, a line and a button each have their own colours. A palette step such as `--ig-gray-600` is raw material: it names a shade, not a job, so it is wrong as soon as the design changes. Write `color: var(--igd-color-foreground-faint);`, not `color: var(--ig-gray-600);`. The check reports it as `raw-palette`.
2. **Say what a space is.** Padding, a vertical margin and a gap or an inline margin each have their own sizes. Naming the kind of space lets padding and gaps be tuned apart later. Write `padding: var(--igd-space-inset-md);`, not `padding: var(--igd-space-md);`. The check reports it as `spacing-role`.
3. **Never type a colour.** Not even one that looks right. When no colour fits, say which one is missing. Write `color: var(--igd-color-foreground-action);`, not `color: #1a5fff;`. The check reports it as `colour-literal`, only with `--strict`.
4. **Use one name for both variants of the theme.** A colour already has a light and a dark value and switches by itself. Do not write the light and the dark variant by hand. Write `background: var(--igd-color-background-card);`, not `background: light-dark(#fff, #1c1c1c);`. The check reports it as `colour-literal`, only with `--strict`.
5. **Resize with a dial, never inside a component.** A dial on the page or on one region makes everything in it denser, rounder or flatter at once. A component never changes a size step itself. Write `<section style="--ig-spacing: 0.5">`, not `.card { --igd-space-md: 8px; }`. The check does not report it.
6. **Widths and heights are yours to type.** They belong to the layout, not to the design system. Do not borrow a spacing step for a size. Write `max-width: 24rem;`, not `max-width: var(--igd-space-6xl);`. The check does not report it.

Also:

- A custom property is `--igd-*` when the design system defines it and `--ig-*` only when the `igniteui-theming` engine emits that exact name.
- Padding uses `--igd-space-inset-*`, vertical margins `--igd-space-stack-*`, gaps and inline margins `--igd-space-gap-*`.
- Hover, active and focus colours are derived from their base token. Override the base on a scope and the states follow.
- A component puts `data-ig-scope` on its root element, so a dial (`--ig-size`, `--ig-spacing`, `--ig-radius-factor` and `--ig-elevation-factor`) set on any ancestor reaches it. Set a dial on the root or on a `data-ig-scope` element.
- When no token fits, do not invent a value that looks like one. Say which token is missing.
- Do not add a fallback to a token read, `var(--igd-color-foreground-subtle, #333)`: the check skips a `var()` with a fallback, so a typo in its name goes unreported.

## Checking a site

Run `npx ig-design-system check src`. It exits with 1 when it finds:

- `unknown-token`: a var(--igd-*) that neither the design system nor the site declares
- `raw-palette`: a palette step that site code reads, such as var(--ig-gray-700)
- `palette-override`: a palette step that site code declares, such as --ig-primary-500
- `spacing-role`: a raw spacing step on padding, a margin or a gap, where a spacing role belongs
- `colour-literal`: a hex colour typed in by hand (only with `--strict`)

`--ignore <text>` skips every path that contains the text. The check does not report:

- a `var()` with a fallback, which it reads as a hook a page may set; a typo in its name goes unreported
- a spacing role in the wrong property, such as a gap role on padding
- a design-system token set on an element
- a raw spacing step inside an HTML `style` attribute
- widths, heights and offsets, which are typed by hand
- Markdown files

## How to read a colour name

`color-{property}-{job}-{emphasis}-{state}`, read as a sentence: `color-foreground-link-hover` is the foreground colour of a link, on hover. A component's own colour reads `{component}-{part}-{property}-{state}`: `badge-new-foreground`.

- `foreground`: anything drawn on a background: text, icons, lines inside a component
- `background`: a fill: a page, a band, a card, a button
- `border`: the edge of a box or a control
- `focus`: the keyboard focus ring
- `accent`: a brand colour for graphics: gradients, tiles, stat numbers

Emphasis: `strong` (more contrast than the default), `default` (the usual choice), `subtle` (less contrast: supporting text, a quiet line), `faint` (the least contrast: captions, small labels), `inverse` (for an area that stays dark in both variants, such as the footer; never on a light surface). A state comes last: `hover` (on hover), `active` (while pressed), `selected` (chosen, such as the current tab), `disabled` (not available). A colour on a fill says so: `color-foreground-on-action` is the label on `color-background-action`. A name never uses `text` (it says foreground), `icon` (it says foreground), `surface` (it says background), `muted` (it says faint or subtle), `primary` (it says a job word, such as action), `secondary` (it says a job word), `alt` (it says a job word), `pressed` (it says active).

## What is in it

- Colour: 109 tokens, plus 101 engine palette steps a site does not read
- Spacing: 45 tokens
- Radius: 7 tokens
- Size: 40 tokens
- Shadow: 41 tokens
- Opacity: 10 tokens
- Font weight: 6 tokens
- Gradient: 8 tokens
- Breakpoint: 4 tokens
- Layer: 8 tokens
- Type: 15 roles (`--igd-type-<role>-font-family`, `-font-size`, `-font-weight`, `-line-height`, `-letter-spacing`, `-text-transform`) and the classes `.igd-type-<role>`

## Writing a component

The same in every framework and every repository: plain HTML, Astro, React, Angular, a web component. It applies to every component built on the design system, not only to Ignite UI components.

1. Put `data-ig-scope` on the root element of the component. The design system calculates its tokens on the root of the page and on each `data-ig-scope` element. With the attribute, a dial set on any ancestor reaches the component, as it reaches an Ignite UI component. Without it, the component keeps the values of the page.
2. A component with shadow DOM puts the attribute on its host element. The stylesheet of the page does not reach inside a shadow root.
3. Style the component with the rules above: spacing roles, semantic colours, type classes, typed widths and heights.
4. Do not set a dial or a spacing, size or radius step inside the component. The page sets dials.

`docs/examples/card.html` is a card written this way, in plain HTML and CSS, with its rules in `docs/examples/card.css`. Its second card sits in a section that sets two dials.

```css
/* A card written to the rules of the design system. card.html loads it; the guide and llms.txt print it. */
.card {
  display: grid;
  /* Widths, heights and offsets are not tokens. */
  max-width: 24rem;
  /* Roles, not raw steps: inset for padding, gap for gaps, stack for vertical margins. */
  gap: var(--igd-space-gap-sm);
  padding: var(--igd-space-inset-lg);
  border: var(--igd-border-width-default) solid var(--igd-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--igd-radius-card);
  background: var(--igd-color-background-card);
  color: var(--igd-color-foreground-default);
}

.card:hover {
  box-shadow: var(--igd-shadow-card-hover);
}

.card__title {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--igd-color-foreground-heading);
}

/* Text in the action colour reads color-foreground-action; its hover is a token too. */
.card__link {
  color: var(--igd-color-foreground-action);
}

.card__link:hover {
  color: var(--igd-color-foreground-link-hover);
}
```

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Card: a component on the design system</title>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../dist/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="../../dist/theme.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="card.css">
</head>
<body>

<!-- The root element of the component carries data-ig-scope. -->
<article class="card" data-ig-scope id="default">
  <h3 class="card__title igd-type-title-sm">Design values</h3>
  <p class="igd-type-body-md">No dial is set above this card.</p>
  <a class="card__link igd-type-label-md" href="#default">Read more</a>
</article>

<!-- A dial on any ancestor reaches the card, because the card's root is a scope. -->
<section style="--ig-spacing: 0.5; --ig-radius-factor: 0">
  <article class="card" data-ig-scope id="compact">
    <h3 class="card__title igd-type-title-sm">Half the spacing, the smallest radius</h3>
    <p class="igd-type-body-md">The section sets two dials. The card follows them.</p>
    <a class="card__link igd-type-label-md" href="#compact">Read more</a>
  </article>
</section>

</body>
</html>
```
